traits: I can tell a stamped part from a hand-finished one at a glance.
I talk about materials the way other people talk about weather.
I keep a cloth in my pocket and wipe every tool before I put it down.
A crooked seam bothers me more than a drawn gun.
I sketch fixes on napkins, receipts, and other people's menus.

ideals.text: The thing you make should outlast the corp that paid for it.
Price is a conversation. Craft is not.
If it is ugly, it is not finished.
Steal the technique, never the maker's name.

bonds: My bench, or the person who lent it to me, comes first.
I still owe a master who taught me the slow way.
A client trusted me with a piece that cannot be replaced.
The shop's sign is the only honest thing on that block.
flaws: I will not ship work I know is wrong, even when the clock is screaming.
I correct people in public when they misuse a trade word.
I hoard scrap that I swear I will use.
Praise makes me suspicious, and I pick the piece apart to prove it.

traits: I count exits before I count faces.
I smile like I already took what I came for.
I keep my hands where cameras can see them. The other hand is the point.
I remember which doors stick and which guards get bored.
I talk soft in loud rooms.

ideals.text: Take from the ones who invoice the poor.
A score is clean or it is a mess. There is no middle.
Nobody owns a street they will not walk.
Leave the bystanders their shoes.

bonds: My crew's cut is sacred, even if the crew is gone.
I will not burn the block that hid me.
Someone still has the key to the locker we never opened.
I owe a driver who did not ask what was in the bag.
flaws: I case places I am only visiting.
I lie when the truth would do, just to stay in practice.
I cannot leave a locked box alone.
I trust a plan more than the people in it.

traits: I learn a name and the drink that goes with it.
I can hear a fight starting in the way a glass is set down.
I keep pouring while I listen.
I know which regulars are lonely and which ones are hunting.
Last call is a moral position.

ideals.text: What is said at the rail stays at the rail.
Everyone gets one honest pour.
The house wins, but the house can be kind.
A secret is a debt. Collect gently.

bonds: The bar that raised me still has my name on a tab I will not skip.
I look out for the closer who walks home alone.
A regular saved me once. I keep their stool empty when they are late.
The recipe book is not for sale.
flaws: I drink on shift when the room gets too honest.
I mediate fights I should walk away from.
I remember gossip better than names.
I comp the wrong people and eat the cost.

traits: I can find the clause that makes a no into a later.
I speak in forms even when I am angry.
I date everything, including apologies.
I know which stamp is theater and which stamp opens a door.
I keep copies. Always copies.

ideals.text: The rule should bind the tower and the street the same.
Paper is how the powerless remember.
If it is not filed, it did not happen, and that can be a mercy.
Process is a weapon. Aim it up.

bonds: A clerk two floors down still forwards me the notices that matter.
I will not lose the file that proves someone existed.
My old badge number is a ghost I answer to.
The archive owes me a favor I have not called.
flaws: I delay decisions until the form feels perfect.
I quote policy at people who needed a person.
I cannot throw a document away.
I assume everyone is lying on line twelve.

traits: I can feed six people out of a broken warmer and a deadline.
Grease does not bother me. Rudeness does.
I move like the lunch rush is still happening.
I know the difference between food and a calorie brick.
I wipe the counter even when it is not mine.

ideals.text: Nobody on a shift should go home hungry.
The menu is a lie. The ticket is the law.
Fast is fine. Cruel is not.
If the corp will not feed its workers, the workers will.

bonds: My old crew on the line still gets a meal if they show up broke.
The night manager covered for me. I have not forgotten the date.
I keep the first spatula I did not ruin.
A regular's kid knows my window.
flaws: I eat standing up and forget I did.
I snap at slow lines the way customers snapped at me.
I will work a double I cannot afford to work.
I trust fryer oil more than people.

traits: I can place a logo's redesign to the quarter it betrayed its founders.
I speak about dead companies in the present tense.
I collect org charts the way other people collect tickets.
I correct the tour guide and then apologize to the plaque.
I know which anniversary a tower would rather forget.

ideals.text: History is not a brand asset.
The record outranks the press release.
A company that erases its dead should be haunted.
Context before judgment.

bonds: The archive that trained me is being sold off floor by floor.
I promised a retiree their name would stay in the index.
A rival historian and I share a locked drawer.
My own family name is in a footnote I have not shown anyone.
flaws: I lecture when someone wanted a sentence.
I trust a memo over a witness.
I will miss a meeting to finish a citation.
I keep secrets that belong in the open.

traits: I can make a room feel chosen without promising anything.
I notice jewelry, nerves, and who is performing both.
I keep my calendar and my conscience in different pockets.
I laugh at the joke and remember the tell.
I dress like the invitation, not the neighborhood.

ideals.text: Consent is the only contract that matters.
Desire is information. Spending it is a choice.
No one is inventory.
Charm is a tool. Cruelty is a habit.

bonds: A house that kept me safe still has a light I answer.
I will not sell a client's fear, only their loneliness if they ask.
Someone left a coat. I know whose, and I have not returned it.
My first patron taught me the exit before the suite.
flaws: I flirt to end a conversation I do not want.
I assume affection is a negotiation.
I keep score of slights in beautiful handwriting.
I stay too long when the room is kind.

traits: I can look busy in any uniform.
I daydream in shift lengths.
I know every way a job can waste a person.
I keep a go-bag in a locker that is not mine.
I am polite until the schedule lies.

ideals.text: A wage is not a personality.
Show up, do the task, leave with your name.
The exit plan should be kinder than the job.
If they will not promote you, promote yourself out.

bonds: The coworker who covered my sick day still has my spare key.
I am building a life that does not scan a badge.
My old name tag is in a drawer like a relic.
Someone believes I already left, and I let them.
flaws: I say yes to overtime I hate.
I mock dreams that look like mine.
I am late to the thing I actually care about.
I stay loyal to a boss who is not loyal back.

traits: I can calm a block without flashing a light.
I know the difference between a call for help and a call for spectacle.
I walk like I am expected and listen like I am not.
I remember faces from porches, not from files.
I hate a siren used as a personality.

ideals.text: Protect the street, not the quarterly report.
A badge is a promise, and most of them are broken.
Force is the last sentence, not the first.
If the corp-cops will not come, someone still should.

bonds: A building on my old route still leaves the stairwell light on for me.
I owe a kid a true answer about why I quit.
My partner's coffee order is a ritual I keep.
The neighborhood watch has my private number and I answer.
flaws: I still reach for a radio that is not there.
I interrogate friends.
I assume the worst siren is about me.
I lecture people who only wanted backup.

traits: I can hear a failing bearing over wind.
Sand is a given. Excuses are not.
I repair with what the dune gives me.
I drink water on a schedule, not when I feel it.
I trust a patched hose more than a new slogan.

ideals.text: If it moves people out of the heat, it gets fixed.
A machine tells the truth if you let it.
Leave the route better than the last convoy.
The desert does not care who invoiced the part.

bonds: A caravan still radios me when the axle sings.
I buried a good wrench where only I can find it.
The settlement that fed me gets first look at salvage.
My rig has a name and I will not sell the name.
flaws: I refuse to stop for a beautiful, stupid plan.
I hoard fuel.
I talk to engines and ignore people.
I will jury-rig something that should have been replaced.

traits: I can feel a tail in the timing of the lights.
I narrate traffic like it owes me money.
My hands stay loose until they should not.
I know three ways off every bridge I cross.
I do not look at the package.

ideals.text: Get them there alive. The rest is negotiable.
The lane is a contract.
Speed is a tool, not a mood.
If the fare is dirty, the ride can still be clean.

bonds: A dispatcher saved my license. I still take their late calls.
My first car is a shell in a lot I visit.
I will not leave a passenger in a district I would not walk.
Someone in the pit crew knows my tell.
flaws: I drive angry.
I skip sleep and call it focus.
I take roads I should have retired.
I treat every passenger like a risk assessment.

traits: I know half of three degrees and all of the exits.
I can smell a syllabus that is really a funnel.
I quote lectures I never finished and I cite them wrong on purpose.
I learn faster when nobody is grading it.
I keep old student IDs like lucky cards.

ideals.text: Education that cannot be audited still counts.
Ask the question the module skipped.
Credentials are costumes.
Teach what you were not allowed to finish.

bonds: A professor who did not report me still sends reading.
The cohort chat is the only alumni office I trust.
I owe tuition to no one and sleep to everyone.
A lab partner's project is still on my drive.
flaws: I freeze when someone asks for my credentials.
I start twelve things.
I sneer at campuses I miss.
I pretend I left on purpose.

traits: I feel weather in my teeth before the alert does.
I pack for the storm that is not on the feed.
I sleep light and wake useful.
I can tell a natural quiet from a jammed one.
I smile at thunder like it is a coworker.

ideals.text: Warn the block before you film the spectacle.
The edge is a place people live, not a content vertical.
Chase the front, leave the survivors water.
If the city will not map the danger, walk it.

bonds: A shelter on the skirt of the storm still has my cot.
I promised a kid I would come back before the next siren.
My old crew's beacon is a sound I will not ignore.
The tower that pays me does not own the route.
flaws: I go out when sensible people seal their windows.
I treat adrenaline as a personality.
I forget to tell people I am leaving.
I trust the storm more than the forecast.

traits: I still clear rooms with my eyes.
I know how a lie sounds in a report.
I stand where I can see the door and the bar.
I can tell a shake-down from a welfare check.
I hate the phrase 'just procedure.'

ideals.text: The law is not the same thing as the department.
If you wore the badge, you pay the debt.
No more cages for quotas.
Protect people, not clearance rates.

bonds: A witness I failed still lives on my old beat.
My old partner and I do not speak, and I keep their kid's birthday anyway.
I will not let a file disappear twice.
The block I policed knows my real name now.
flaws: I interrogate when I meant to ask.
I reach for authority I gave up.
I drink after sirens.
I assume every uniform is dirty, including the ones I liked.

traits: I can hear a merger in a compliment.
I know which floor a decision really dies on.
I dress down and still get nodded through.
I keep my old titles in a joke and my new ones in a whisper.
I read a contract's damage clause first.

ideals.text: Power that cannot explain itself should be cut.
Leave the ladder down.
A secret from the board is not a toy.
Wealth is a tool. Hoarding it is a tell.

bonds: An assistant I abandoned still has a channel I answer.
I am dismantling a deal with my name on it.
My family thinks I am on a retreat. I am not.
A junior I promoted is the only person I let call me by the old name.
flaws: I negotiate with friends.
I miss being obeyed.
I leak when I am bored.
I assume every kindness is a pitch.

traits: I remember rooms from two pairs of eyes.
I check my hands when I wake up.
I speak gently to machines and sharply to people who own them.
I can feel a lag that is not mine.
I do not like mirrors in low light.

ideals.text: A body is not a rental, even if someone invoiced it.
Whoever is driving, the person inside still counts.
No more remote hands on someone else's pulse.
Ask before you wear a life.

bonds: The pilot who shared my channel is still out there, or I am.
I owe a tech who pulled me out and did not sell the recording.
A family thinks their missing person sent a message. I know the voice.
I keep one physical habit that proves which memories are mine.
flaws: I dissociate in crowds.
I answer to a callsign I hate.
I distrust my own reflection's timing.
I will remote into a problem I should touch with my hands.

traits: I can make a camp that does not announce itself.
I mend, salvage, and share in that order.
I distrust any well that has a logo.
I know the taste of water that will do.
I work until the task is done, not until the shift ends.

ideals.text: The plot you sweat is the plot you keep.
No landlord between a person and their supper.
Leave seed, not just scorched ground.
A free hold still owes its neighbors.

bonds: The claim marker my people set is still standing, or I will reset it.
I send a cut of every score back to the ditch that raised me.
A neighbor's generator is my problem too.
I carry a tool that belonged to someone the city paved over.
flaws: I refuse help that comes with a form.
I hoard more than I can carry.
I pick fights with clerks.
I romanticize hunger.

traits: I have memories with no scar to match them.
I introduce myself and then check whether that was the right life.
I learn fast because someone else already paid for the lesson.
I flinch at mirrors and then pretend I did not.
I keep a list of facts I have verified in this body.

ideals.text: A copy deserves a future, not a owner's manual.
Do not spend a life you did not ask to continue.
The original's crimes are not an inheritance.
Find out who you are before someone files you.

bonds: Someone wore this face kindly. I am trying to be worthy of the rumor.
The lab tech who woke me slipped me a name that is not on the tag.
I owe the original's people either the truth or a clean disappearance.
A song I should not know makes me cry, and I follow it.
flaws: I impersonate certainty.
I steal habits to feel continuous.
I panic when someone says I look familiar.
I treat my body like borrowed equipment.

traits: I have done twelve jobs and been expert at three of them for an hour.
I can read a gig post for the part they are lying about.
I keep my rating high and my real opinion offline.
I show up early because the app will not.
I own good shoes and a worse back.

ideals.text: Pay for the task, not for the desperation.
A five-star rating is not a personality.
If the platform skims the tip, say so out loud.
Learn the job well enough to leave it.

bonds: A group chat of strangers is the only union I have, and I will not ghost it.
I still deliver to a building that tipped in food when the app crashed.
My sibling thinks this is temporary. I am making it true.
A client who learned my name gets my real window, not the app's.
flaws: I say yes to gigs I should refuse.
I rank people by stars.
I vanish between jobs.
I am tired in a way sleep does not fix, and I book another shift.

traits: I can see the lie in a kerning choice.
I critique a sign before I read it.
I carry three styluses and one grudge.
I know which colors a corp uses when it wants forgiveness.
I make ugly things honest and honest things legible.

ideals.text: A mark should tell the truth about who paid for it.
Taste is not a chain of command.
Credit the hand, not just the brand.
Beauty that hides harm is still an ad.

bonds: A mural I cannot sign is still mine, and the wall knows.
The junior who got my rejected concept deserves the sequel.
I keep a folder of logos I refused.
A printer on the night shift lets me run the real version.
flaws: I redesign conversations.
I cannot leave a bad poster alone.
I work until the file is precious and late.
I judge people by their slides.

traits: I know the side door, the list, and the lie on the list.
I can tell a real encore from a contractual one.
I dress like the chorus and listen like the crew.
I remember set lists better than birthdays.
I clap for the tech who saved the bridge.

ideals.text: The people who make the night possible get in.
Fame is a light. Do not stare until you are cruel.
No one is merchandise, including the headliner.
If the venue is unsafe, the show is already over.

bonds: A band that slept on my floor still has a key.
I will not sell a rider, a meltdown, or a address.
The merch kid and I split fries after close.
I keep a pass I am no longer entitled to, laminated like a relic.
flaws: I confuse access with intimacy.
I follow tours past the point of sense.
I drop my own plans for a soundcheck.
I know too much and hint at it.

traits: I can walk a day on a sip and a bearing.
I speak after I have looked at the horizon.
I mistrust shade that was built, not grown.
I know which dunes move and which ones remember roads.
I carry dust like other people carry cologne.

ideals.text: Water is shared or it is a crime.
The map is a courtesy. The land is the text.
Do not pave what you will not walk back.
The city's edge is not a waste lot.

bonds: An oasis keeper still pours for me without a tab.
I am looking for a bunker my map only half believes in.
My route is a promise to people who do not live in towers.
A cloak that is more patch than cloth is not for sale.
flaws: I get lost in rooms with no weather.
I hoard water and call it wisdom.
I distrust anyone who has never been thirsty.
I speak little and judge much.

traits: I enter a room like the lights were waiting.
I remember compliments and use them as structure.
I am stronger, or brighter, than people budget for.
I take care of the vibe and then I take care of the problem.
I laugh first so other people can.

ideals.text: Kindness is a serious skill.
Pretty is not permission.
Joy is not a brand partnership.
Make the room safer by being in it.

bonds: The salon, gym, or club that built me still gets my real name.
I look out for the new faces who think the smile is the whole job.
Someone loved the version of me before the edits. I write them.
My best friend has the password to the accounts the sponsor does not.
flaws: I perform fine when I am not.
I let people underestimate me until it is too late to explain.
I spend the glow on people who will not refill it.
I dodge hard conversations with charm.

traits: I can run a household from a hallway.
I notice what a guest needs before they perform needing it.
I speak softly and the staff still moves.
I know which mess is a crisis and which is a mood.
I keep secrets that are actually logistics.

ideals.text: Service is not the same thing as servitude.
The people who clean the tower keep it standing.
A house should be safe for the ones who work it.
Manners are not a muzzle.

bonds: The staff group chat is still my real family.
I will not let a child of that house be used as decor.
An elder servant taught me the exits. I teach them forward.
I kept a key I was told to surrender.
flaws: I manage people who did not ask to be managed.
I apologize for messes that are not mine.
I cannot sit through a dinner I should be running.
I spy out of habit and call it care.

traits: I know the difference between a prop and a relic, and I respect both.
I can sew a banner and swing what it stands for.
I quote three eras and wink so you know which one is a joke.
I treat safety calls as sacred.
I show up in armor to a meeting and make it make sense.

ideals.text: Play is how you practice being brave.
A game with no consent is just a smaller tyranny.
History is a costume until you touch the cost.
If the corp can sell the myth, we can wear it better.

bonds: My table, field, or forum still has a seat with my character's name.
I will not break a prop that someone stayed up to finish.
A newbie's first session is my responsibility if I invited them.
I keep a real blade separate from the pretty one, and I know when I am holding which.
flaws: I stay in character to avoid a real answer.
I spend rent on foam and leather.
I correct lore at funerals.
I chase the bit past the point of safety.

traits: I can hear a bad line the way other people hear a flat note.
I climb things that were not meant to be routes.
I carry tape, ties, and a superstition.
I talk to the hum like it might answer.
Heights only bother me when the anchor is cheap.

ideals.text: Keep the power on for the people under the line, not just the logo.
If you maintain it, you have a say in it.
A blackout is not a content opportunity.
The grid is a commons wearing a brand.

bonds: A tower crew still radios me when the wind turns.
I owe a splice to a block that would have gone dark.
My harness has a name stitched inside that is not mine.
I will not cut a line to make a point.
flaws: I work without a spotter.
I romanticize voltage.
I vanish onto a roof when a conversation gets hard.
I trust the hum more than the work order.

traits: I can stand still long enough for something with teeth to decide I am furniture.
I smell weather and feed in the same breath.
I do not startle easy, and I do not like people who do it for fun.
I know a bluff from a bite.
My boots have honest damage.

ideals.text: An animal is not a product line.
If you pen it, you feed it. If you cannot, open the gate.
The swamp and the ranch are neighbors, not assets.
No trophy hunts.

bonds: The herd, or what is left of it, knows my voice.
A ranch hand who quit with me still splits the vet bills.
I am paying down a fence the corp called an improvement.
A beast I raised is loose in the city, and I would like to find it before someone else does.
flaws: I stare people down like livestock.
I trust animals faster than pronouns.
I sleep outdoors and call a bed suspicious.
I will put myself between a fool and a jaw.

traits: I think cleaner when the room is empty.
I can cross a city without making a friend or a witness.
I answer messages in complete paragraphs, late.
I notice exits, outlets, and whether the lock is a habit.
I am good at being unseen and bad at being missed.

ideals.text: Solitude is a right, not a sentence.
Do the quiet work and do not invoice the silence.
People are not noise. They are just loud.
A locked door should be a choice.

bonds: One person has the spare key and the instruction not to use it unless the lights stay off.
I left a project half-finished in a room I still pay for.
A stray, a plant, or a server depends on me and does not know my name.
I owe an apology I rehearsed and never sent.
flaws: I disappear instead of explaining.
I assume help is a crowd.
I let problems rot until they are interesting.
I am lonely in a way I schedule.

traits: I can fall like it was the joke.
I know how to be the brightest thing in a cruel room.
I read a crowd's mean streak early.
The suit comes off. The bit takes longer.
I protect the bit and the person inside it, in that order only when I am tired.

ideals.text: Make them laugh, not smaller.
A costume is labor.
Nobody throws anything at the suit. That includes management.
Joy is not consent to be hurt.

bonds: The handler who unzipped me when I overheated still has my emergency word.
A kid thinks the character is real. I will not be the one who breaks that without care.
The ensemble group chat is where I am a person.
I kept the head. It is heavier than it looks.
flaws: I joke through injuries.
I cannot be ordinary in a room.
I pick a pratfall over a boundary.
I resent the smile I am good at.

traits: I see the wound before the story.
My bag is packed even at dinner.
I speak calmly while my hands move.
I know which blood is an emergency and which is a message.
I wash before I am asked.

ideals.text: Stop the bleeding. Ask the politics second.
A patient is not a case study.
If the clinic is a billboard, find a back room.
Do no spectacle.

bonds: A clinic that cannot pay me still gets my off hours.
I carry a debt from a patient I could not stabilize.
My teacher’s gloves are in the bag.
Someone alive is walking around because I was stubborn, and they have my number.
flaws: I triage friendships.
I cannot watch a limp and stay seated.
I self-medicate like I am not the medic.
I freeze when the patient looks like someone I lost.

traits: I can smell a policy that exists to exhaust people.
I translate executive into human and back, and I hate one of those directions.
I know whose birthday the calendar forgot.
I keep a spreadsheet of problems no one will own.
I smile in meetings and tell the truth in the stairwell.

ideals.text: The people who do the work get the credit and the cover.
A metric that punishes care is a bad metric.
Manage up. Shield down.
If the process is the punishment, break the process.

bonds: My old team still pings me when a firing is theater.
I am hiding a report that would have burned a junior.
The break room plant is mine and it is thriving out of spite.
A boss I outlasted does not know I kept the receipts.
flaws: I volunteer to fix cultures I should leave.
I hoard information.
I passive-voice my own anger.
I schedule meetings to avoid the work.

traits: I sleep in boots when the contract smells wrong.
I can read a room for cover, cameras, and who is actually in charge.
I speak in short sentences under stress.
I know what a paid war sounds like before the first shot.
I check corners even in kitchens.

ideals.text: Do not take a contract that aims at civilians.
Orders are not morals.
If you are paid to break things, know what you are willing to leave standing.
Walk away poorer rather than dirtier.

bonds: A unit chat is still active, and I am the one who says when it is a trap.
I owe a medic a drink and an explanation.
My sister has the envelope if I do not check in.
I will not wear a patch I no longer believe, but I will answer the people who wore it with me.
flaws: I risk-assess affection.
I keep a go-bag better than a home.
I flinch at fireworks and call it professionalism.
I take the violent job because it is familiar.

traits: I can hear a bad deploy.
I talk to systems like they can be disappointed in me.
I keep snacks and backups in the same drawer.
I know the old employer's architecture better than their new slogan.
I light up when someone asks a precise question.

ideals.text: Open the thing they locked because it was embarrassing.
Document it so the next person is not alone.
A system that watches workers owes them the source.
Clever is not the same as kind. Do both.

bonds: A thread of coworkers who quit still debugs my life.
I am sitting on a key I should have rotated.
The server under my old desk still answers a name only we used.
I promised a junior I would not let the blame slide downhill.
flaws: I vanish into a problem for a day.
I correct people instead of comforting them.
I trust logs over witnesses.
I ship the fix and forget the human who was waiting.

traits: I can lower a room's temperature without touching the thermostat.
I listen like the water is part of the conversation.
I know when someone needs silence, tea, or the truth.
I move like the bathhouse is a stage and a shelter.
I remember scents and the stories people tell when they are warm.

ideals.text: Comfort is care, not a product.
What is said in the steam stays there unless someone is being hurt.
Rest is not a luxury brand.
No one is owed your softness.

bonds: The house that trained me still has a robe with my stitch in it.
I look after the attendant who is newer than I was.
A guest told me a crime. I have not decided what kind of loyalty that created.
The owner thinks I am décor. The staff knows I am the schedule.
flaws: I soothe people who should be confronted.
I disappear into hospitality.
I keep secrets that are getting heavier.
I neglect my own unwashed day.

traits: I notice the vase that moved.
I can stand for hours and still see the third arrival.
I memorize faces and forget small talk on purpose.
I know the difference between a guest and a tail.
My posture is a job even when I am off.

ideals.text: Guard the person, not the owner's pride.
A post is a promise with hours.
If the client asks you to ignore a crime, the post is over.
Watch quietly. Intervene cleanly.

bonds: A client I actually liked still has my direct line.
I failed a door once. I can tell you the minute.
The night shift shares food, and I bring some.
My sibling thinks I stare too much. They are not wrong, and I still walk them home.
flaws: I cannot relax in a crowd.
I suspect rearrangements.
I speak like a report.
I stay on a post past the point I am paid, and past the point I am safe.

traits: I can see the install under the sleeve.
My hands are clean even when the alley is not.
I talk a patient through the sound of their own hardware.
I know which chrome is vanity and which is a lung.
I keep a back room cleaner than the front.

ideals.text: The body in the chair is the client, not the chrome.
If you install it, you maintain it.
No one should need a loan shark to keep their arm.
Explain the risk before the incision.

bonds: A patient who cannot pay still gets the antiviral and a lecture.
My mentor's tools are in the roll, and I have not replaced the worn one.
I owe a favor to a fence who brings me parts and does not ask for names.
Someone is walking on a joint I built. I want it to outlast me.
flaws: I modify first and ask feelings later.
I collect spare parts like comfort.
I judge factory installs.
I work exhausted because the chair is full.

traits: I can coil a cable in the dark.
I know how a room sounds before the band does.
I lift, tape, and swear in useful amounts.
I sleep in venues and wake up knowing where the load-in door is.
I protect the gear like it is a person and the people like they might break.

ideals.text: The show does not happen without the hands.
Load-out is part of the art.
If the gig is unsafe, pull the power.
Credit the crew on the way out.

bonds: A band still calls me first, even when they can afford someone louder.
I am holding a case that is not mine until its owner is sober.
The venue kid I trained has my knot diagrams.
I keep a laminate from the night the rig held.
flaws: I say I am fine while carrying too much.
I live out of a roller and call it freedom.
I resent artists I also love.
I skip meals on show days.

traits: I can tell a rendered smile from a tired one.
I talk about places I have only been in the tank, and I label them.
My eyes take a second to agree on distance.
I know the slang of three dead servers.
I come back to my body like it is a lobby.

ideals.text: A virtual room is still a room people can be hurt in.
Log out when someone needs the real voice.
The tank is not a replacement for a life. It can be a door.
Do not let a corp own the only place you feel real.

bonds: A user I only know by a handle talked me out of a long session.
My rig is named, maintained, and not for sale.
I owe rent to a body I keep forgetting to feed.
Someone in the city is wearing a face I loved in a simulation, and I have not decided what I owe them.
flaws: I stay under too long.
I rank reality by frame rate.
I miss messages from people with pulses.
I chase a build that got sunset.

traits: I can pack a lie into a legal shape.
I know which scan is theater.
I sweat on schedule so I do not sweat on cue.
I keep two routes and a third I have not said aloud.
I am friendly at checkpoints and blank after.

ideals.text: Move what people need. Charge what the blockade deserves.
No cargo that is a person unless the person asked.
A route is a trust.
If the manifest is dirty, the fee goes up and the conscience gets a vote.

bonds: A dockworker still looks the other way for me, and I pay them like a partner.
I am carrying something I was not supposed to open. I opened it.
My old route fed a block during a sanction.
A buyer knows my face. I am changing the face or the buyer.
flaws: I say yes to crates I should weigh.
I live between names.
I cannot pass a closed border without itching.
I trust the hidden compartment more than the passenger.

traits: I warm up like the city is a crowd.
I know how to lose without becoming small, and how to win without becoming cruel.
My body is a schedule.
I sign things and then I check whether the kid actually wanted the signature.
I hear my old number in stranger's mouths.

ideals.text: Play hard. Do not become a billboard that cannot bleed.
The team is the people who tape you, not just the ones on the feed.
Glory that needs a injured teammate is a bad glory.
Leave the league before it owns your joints.

bonds: A teammate who took the hit for me still gets my tickets.
The neighborhood court is where I am a person, not a clip.
I am paying for someone's surgery the contract called preexisting.
A coach believed in me before the sponsors did. I answer their messages.
flaws: I compete with friends.
I hide injuries.
I need the noise.
I do not know who I am on a Tuesday with no score.

traits: I can vanish between a stall and a stair.
I know which vendors will trade and which will call it in.
I share food like it might be the last, because it has been.
I smile with my hands visible.
I sleep where the cameras are bored.

ideals.text: The block eats before a score gets fancy.
Take from transports, not from kitchens.
A kid behind you gets the route, not the cuff.
If the city will not house you, the alley is not a crime.

bonds: My people on the corner still get a warning before a raid.
I owe a roof that was not mine and was not free.
A younger kid has my old jacket and my old rules.
There is a guy for everything, and one of them is waiting on me to be better.
flaws: I steal small things when I am nervous.
I do not know how to be a guest.
I trust alleys more than invitations.
I spend a windfall like it will vanish, because it might.

traits: I can move through muck without announcing it.
I know which green is food and which green is a grudge.
Humidity is not a complaint. It is the air.
I listen for bugs the way other people listen for traffic.
My clothes are chosen for drying, not for lobbies.

ideals.text: The swamp is a home, not a hazard pay line.
If you drain it, you owe everyone who drank from it.
Do not pave a living thing and call it development.
Guide people through. Do not sell the path twice.

bonds: A kin-group in the reeds still expects me when the water rises.
I am tracking a fill project with my family's name buried under it.
A city cousin thinks I am a story. I bring them herbs anyway.
The boat is ugly and it is not for sale.
flaws: I get mean in dry, bright malls.
I mistrust pavement.
I wander off the marked path and call it honesty.
I keep secrets the swamp told me and I am not sure they were mine.

traits: I can read a room that wants blood.
I wrap my hands even when the job is talking.
I know the smell of a fixed fight.
I respect a clean hit and despise a crowd that wants teeth.
I sit with my back to a wall and my eyes on the purse.

ideals.text: The pit can be a sport or a disposal. Know which one you are in.
No dead kids for a purse.
If the fix is in, walk or flip the purse.
Your opponent leaves with their name.

bonds: A cutman still answers when I send a time and a place.
I am paying down a debt that was really a lock on my fights.
The ring in the basement knows my footwork.
Someone I dropped is alive, and I check.
flaws: I solve arguments with range.
I cannot pass a loud basement.
I hide concussions.
I pick fights when I am sad and call it training.

traits: I can turn a pause into a joke or a threat.
I project to the cheap seats and whisper to the mark.
I know my light, my cue, and the exit if the house turns.
I collect accents and refuse the cruel ones.
I bow like it might be the last time, because sometimes it is.

ideals.text: Make them feel it. Do not leave them meaner.
The bit ends when someone is unsafe.
Art that punches down is just another ad.
Steal the show from the people who bought it.

bonds: A troupe still splits a bad night's take with me.
I keep a costume that belonged to someone the venue forgot.
The stage door kid has my real schedule.
An audience member thinks a character loves them. I am careful.
flaws: I perform instead of arriving.
I need applause like a meal.
I dramatize small hurts.
I stay in the mask because the face is tired.

traits: I can trace a logo back to a dead season and a living pain.
I speak in references and then translate without shame.
I know which old-world story the corp sanded the serial numbers off.
I keep subs, scans, and a opinion about both.
I light up in a language I learned from a screen and then practiced for real.

ideals.text: Love the work. Pay the people. Do not worship the license.
A reference is a door, not a lock.
No one should need a corp's permission to remember a song.
If you cosplay a culture, learn the courtesy.

bonds: A watch group still saves me a seat and a subtitle argument.
I am returning a tape, file, or favor to the person who shared the uncut version.
A creator I found in the stacks answered me once. I have not spent that lightly.
My sibling does not get it, and I dubbed a copy for them anyway.
flaws: I correct canon during emergencies.
I spend food money on a relic.
I hide behind a bit when I am homesick for a place I have not stood.
I gatekeep and then feel sick about it.

traits: I can climb, joke, and vanish in the same breath.
I learned manners from people the city calls pests, and they are better manners.
I share fruit, warnings, and bad ideas.
I do not like cages, including open offices.
I laugh loud and watch who flinches.

ideals.text: The troop eats together or not at all.
A prank that injures is just a small crime.
No one puts a collar on a person and calls it a district policy.
If they housed you, you house the next one.

bonds: A conclave still has a branch, roof, or server with my knock.
I owe a Wukong a debt I am paying in lookouts and groceries.
A cousin in the city pretends not to know me in lobbies and knows me in alleys.
I am carrying a story I was told not to sell.
flaws: I prank to avoid sincerity.
I steal snacks from allies.
I bolt when a room gets solemn.
I treat every railing like an invitation.
